blindSummary:
Two penal-code provisions criminalise "sexual acts against nature" and public indecency, and there is no legal gender recognition. Conditions worsened after a major change of government in 2024: a trans advocacy organisation documented "waves of violence" against trans women in this country in the first two months of 2025, implicating both non-state armed groups and security forces in multiple cities, and February 2025 videos showed authorities arresting trans women. Digital targeting (entrapment via apps, extortion) is documented across the conflict period.

For a visitor: active conflict, trans-targeted violence waves, no recourse whatsoever.
blindOutOfScope: General conflict risk affects all; the 2025 trans-women violence waves are trans-specific.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): penal-code provisions criminalise 'sexual acts against nature' and public indecency; no legal gender recognition and no prohibition of nonconsensual intersex interventions; during the 2011-2024 conflict, violence on SOGI grounds escalated - religious-militant groups executed and publicly tortured sexual and gender minorities (particularly queer men and trans women); government forces arrested people on morality charges, committed enforced disappearances and sexual violence in detention.

International human-rights organisation report (April 2018) on LGBT activism across the region: includes this country's penal-code criminalisation and the situation of LGBT people here amid the conflict.

Local news outlet (Oct 2020): LGBT activists at home and abroad fight to have their voices heard - one activist has helped people kicked out of work or home since 2004; in 'gay-friendly' cafes in the capital, friends spoke 'only in whispers'; that activist said the closet door people were put behind must be broken down, because they deserve life.

Newsmagazine (2015): two gay refugees from this country and a neighbouring state testified at the first-ever UN Security Council meeting on LGBT rights (closed session, co-sponsored by two member states) about constant fear of violence and death under authoritarian governments, militant groups and a short-lived militant proto-state.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (June 2010): authorities raided private gay parties, arresting over 25 men - charged with 'homosexual acts', drugs, or 'obscene' parties; families refused to pay bail; police monitor cruising areas; a regional LGBT rights group called for repeal of the 'antiquated' criminalisation in the 1949 penal code.
blindTangential: The penal-code provisions criminalise “sexual acts against nature” — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
